microtheory.name: psychology_foundation
microtheory.definition: Foundational psychology as the substrate's mid-level explanatory layer between neuroscience and behaviour. Where neuroscience describes mechanism (synapses, plasticity, microcircuits), psychology describes the functions that mechanism gives rise to: perception, memory, attention, emotion, motivation, learning, social behaviour, individual differences, development. Many of the substrate's drives + dynamics are formal restatements of psychological constructs (curiosity = information-gap theory; coherence = cognitive consistency; ΔF = expectation violation). This Mt names those constructs explicitly so the substrate's introspection can trace its drives to their psychological origin and so analogical_transfer can mine psychology for further moves. Distinct from the existing smaller `psychology` Mt (theory-of-mind focused) — this is the broader foundational layer.

concepts.name: mind
concepts.definition: The set of cognitive faculties: perception, cognition, emotion, motivation, memory. The substrate analogue is the substrate's graph + cortices + drives.

concepts.name: consciousness
concepts.definition: Subjective awareness — that there is 'something it is like' to be the agent (Nagel 1974). The hard problem. Substrate analogue: the substrate's introspection produces graph-resident records of its own state.

concepts.name: self_concept
concepts.definition: An organised set of beliefs about one's own attributes, capabilities, values, identities. Distinguishes 'me' from 'not me'. Substrate analogue: the substrate's identity field + foundational Mts marked update_policy='frozen'.

concepts.name: schema
concepts.definition: Bartlett 1932, Piaget. An organised body of knowledge that guides perception, memory, expectation. Substrate analogue: a Mt — a coherent bundle of concepts that scaffolds related learning.

concepts.name: attention
concepts.definition: Selective allocation of processing resources to a subset of available information. James 1890. Substrate analogue: substrate's drive-priority biasing of reflex selection.

concepts.name: perception
concepts.definition: Active construction of representations from sensory input. Helmholtz's unconscious inference. Substrate analogue: the substrate's sensory cortices.

concepts.name: memory
concepts.definition: Encoding + storage + retrieval. Atkinson + Shiffrin 1968. Substrate analogue: substrate's events + Mt-resident knowledge + the consolidation pathway.

concepts.name: learning
concepts.definition: Change in behaviour or knowledge as a function of experience. Substrate analogue: substrate's structural updates — new edges + concept-invention + correction firing.

concepts.name: thinking
concepts.definition: Manipulation of mental representations. Substrate analogue: substrate's runtime evaluation of Term-trees + cortex assessment loops.

concepts.name: language
concepts.definition: Symbolic communication. Chomsky's generative grammar. Substrate analogue: substrate's lexical access faculty + speech cortex.

concepts.name: decision_making
concepts.definition: Selection of one option from alternatives based on values + beliefs + uncertainty. Substrate analogue: substrate's ActionSpec selection under drive-priority weighting.

concepts.name: problem_solving
concepts.definition: Goal-directed search through a problem space. Newell + Simon 1972. Substrate analogue: substrate's curiosity-drive exploration via what-if probes.

concepts.name: reasoning
concepts.definition: Drawing inferences from premises. Deductive, inductive, abductive. Substrate analogue: substrate's rule walks + derivation_mechanism.

concepts.name: emotion
concepts.definition: Multi-component reaction (subjective feeling + physiological response + behaviour) to evaluated events. Substrate analogue: substrate's coherence-drive amplitude on high-magnitude ΔF events.

concepts.name: affect
concepts.definition: Valenced state. Russell's circumplex: valence × arousal. Substrate analogue: substrate's drive-balance — net positive or negative tendency.

concepts.name: mood
concepts.definition: Slow-changing background affect. Substrate analogue: substrate's baseline temperature β slowly modulating across loops.

concepts.name: motivation
concepts.definition: Internal state that energises + directs behaviour toward goals. Self-determination theory (Deci+Ryan). Substrate analogue: substrate's drive ensemble.

concepts.name: drive
concepts.definition: Internal state of need that motivates behaviour. Hull 1943. Substrate analogue: literally substrate's drive_curiosity, drive_coherence, drive_parsimony, drive_stability, drive_discrimination, drive_coverage.

concepts.name: intrinsic_motivation
concepts.definition: Engagement for the activity's own sake. Deci+Ryan: autonomy + competence + relatedness. Substrate analogue: substrate's curiosity-drive.

concepts.name: extrinsic_motivation
concepts.definition: Engagement for external reward. Substrate analogue: substrate's correction signals.

concepts.name: cognitive_dissonance
concepts.definition: Festinger 1957. Aversive state when beliefs/attitudes/behaviour are inconsistent. Drives belief change. Substrate analogue: substrate's coherence-drive — frustration from inconsistent Mt states.

concepts.name: cognitive_consistency
concepts.definition: The brain's preference for internal consistency among beliefs. Heider's balance theory, Festinger, Newcomb. Substrate analogue: substrate's coherence-between-layers principle.

concepts.name: confirmation_bias
concepts.definition: Tendency to seek/interpret evidence supporting existing beliefs. Wason 1960. Substrate analogue: substrate's identity-field bias toward sustained σ patterns.

concepts.name: motivated_reasoning
concepts.definition: Goal-driven processing where conclusion is set first + evidence is selected to fit. Kunda 1990. Substrate analogue: substrate's frozen Mts resisting disconfirming evidence.

concepts.name: expectation_violation
concepts.definition: When perceived outcome diverges from predicted outcome. Substrate analogue: substrate's ΔF — predicted vs actual basin state.

concepts.name: information_gap
concepts.definition: Loewenstein 1994. Curiosity arises from awareness of a gap between current + desired knowledge. Substrate analogue: substrate's curiosity-drive — high-entropy regions = information gaps.

concepts.name: novelty_preference
concepts.definition: Preference for novel over familiar stimuli. Substrate analogue: substrate's curiosity-drive ranking unseen concepts higher.

concepts.name: surprise
concepts.definition: Cognitive + affective response to unexpected events. Drives memory encoding + attention. Substrate analogue: substrate's high-ΔF events triggering encoding into TheoryEnactmentGap or InsightEvent.

concepts.name: habit
concepts.definition: Automatic, stimulus-triggered behaviour learned through repetition. Wood + Neal 2007. Substrate analogue: substrate's ActionSpec dispatch via runtime_discovery.

concepts.name: skill
concepts.definition: Learned ability to perform an action efficiently. Anderson's ACT-R. Substrate analogue: substrate's FilterSpec emergence from AST-migration.

concepts.name: conditioning
concepts.definition: Learning via stimulus-outcome pairings. Classical (Pavlov), operant (Skinner). Substrate analogue: substrate's covers_correction strengthening when corrections fire successfully.

concepts.name: reinforcement
concepts.definition: Process by which a stimulus increases or decreases the future frequency of a behaviour. Substrate analogue: substrate's RPE-driven update of ActionSpec coverage.

concepts.name: behaviourism
concepts.definition: Watson + Skinner. Only observable stimulus-response is the proper object of psychology. Substrate analogue: NOT the substrate's stance — it explicitly seeds + introspects mental constructs.

concepts.name: cognitive_revolution
concepts.definition: 1950s-60s overthrow of behaviourism. Chomsky, Miller, Neisser. Internal representations + processes become the proper object. Substrate analogue: substrate's whole architecture.

concepts.name: cognitive_architecture
concepts.definition: Formal theory of structure + dynamics of cognition: ACT-R, SOAR, Global Workspace. Substrate analogue: the substrate itself.

concepts.name: trait
concepts.definition: Stable individual differences in patterns of thought, feeling, behaviour. Substrate analogue: per-substrate-instance differences in frozen Mt content + drive ensemble weights.

concepts.name: state
concepts.definition: Temporary condition; contrasts with trait. Same substrate has trait-level Mt structure + state-level σ patterns.

concepts.name: personality
concepts.definition: Pattern of traits, motives, defenses, narratives unique to an individual. Substrate analogue: a saved substrate's full graph state.

concepts.name: development
concepts.definition: Systematic changes in cognition, emotion, behaviour across the lifespan. Piaget, Vygotsky, Erikson. Substrate analogue: substrate's developmental phase transitions + critical periods.

concepts.name: critical_period_psychological
concepts.definition: Limited time window when a specific developmental capability can be acquired. Language critical period 0-7 years. Substrate analogue: substrate's plasticity_override windows.

concepts.name: social_cognition
concepts.definition: How people perceive, interpret, think about others. Substrate analogue: model_understanding Mt in substrate.

concepts.name: theory_of_mind
concepts.definition: Premack + Woodruff 1978. Ability to attribute mental states to others. Develops ~4 yrs. Substrate analogue: substrate's modelling-of-other-Mts capability.

concepts.name: attribution
concepts.definition: How people explain causes of behaviour. Substrate analogue: substrate's causal_influence edge as explanation of σ pattern.

concepts.name: in_group_out_group
concepts.definition: Categorisation of self vs others; in-group favoritism + out-group derogation. Tajfel 1971. Substrate analogue: substrate's identity-protection bias toward concepts within its core Mts.

concepts.name: conformity
concepts.definition: Adjustment of behaviour or beliefs to match group. Asch 1951. Substrate analogue: in collaborative multi-substrate contexts, alignment of Mts.

concepts.name: psychopathology
concepts.definition: Patterns of cognition, emotion, behaviour that cause distress + impairment. Substrate analogue: substrate's failure modes when unchecked.

concepts.name: anxiety
concepts.definition: Anticipatory aversive state about future threats. Substrate analogue: substrate's high-ΔF sustained state without resolution.

concepts.name: depression
concepts.definition: Persistent negative affect + anhedonia + cognitive distortions. Substrate analogue: substrate state where all drives' targets seem unreachable.

concepts.name: ocd
concepts.definition: Intrusive thoughts + repetitive behaviours. Substrate analogue: substrate stuck in repetitive ActionSpec dispatch without coverage progress.

concepts.name: trauma
concepts.definition: Psychological injury from overwhelming experience. PTSD. Substrate analogue: substrate Mts with sustained extreme bias from past event.

concepts.name: wellbeing
concepts.definition: Subjective + eudaimonic forms. Ryff 1989. Substrate analogue: substrate's drive-satisfaction across the ensemble.

concepts.name: flow
concepts.definition: Csikszentmihalyi. Complete absorption with clear goals + immediate feedback + matched challenge-skill. Substrate analogue: substrate's optimal exploration-exploitation balance.

concepts.name: growth_mindset
concepts.definition: Dweck 2006. Belief that abilities can be developed. Substrate analogue: substrate's update_policy='adaptive' Mts.

concepts.name: self_efficacy
concepts.definition: Bandura 1977. Belief in one's ability to succeed. Substrate analogue: substrate's expected-success estimate from past ActionSpec hit rate.

concepts.name: resilience
concepts.definition: Capacity to recover from stress/trauma/setback. Substrate analogue: substrate's recovery from high-frustration states via correction firing.

concepts.name: defense_mechanism
concepts.definition: Freud. Unconscious processes that reduce anxiety. Substrate analogue: substrate's frozen Mts resisting evidence that would threaten identity.

concepts.name: unconscious
concepts.definition: Mental contents inaccessible to consciousness but influential. Substrate analogue: substrate's Python handlers (opaque from graph perspective).

concepts.name: ego
concepts.definition: Freud's mediating structure. Substrate analogue: substrate's ArchitectureCortex + DevelopmentCortex.

concepts.name: schema_therapy
concepts.definition: Young + Klosko + Weishaar 2003. Targets early maladaptive schemas. Substrate analogue: substrate's correction handlers applied to deeply-seeded Mts.

concepts.name: cognitive_restructuring
concepts.definition: Identifying + challenging cognitive distortions. Foundation of CBT. Substrate analogue: substrate's derivation_mechanism surfacing dormant rules.

concepts.name: behaviour_modification
concepts.definition: Changing behaviour through reinforcement principles. Substrate analogue: substrate's ActionSpec coverage update.

concepts.name: exposure
concepts.definition: Graduated exposure to feared stimuli without avoidance. Substrate analogue: substrate's repeated tick exposure → reduced σ excitation.

rules.name: dissonance_drives_consistency_seeking
rules.head: two of the substrate's beliefs are inconsistent
rules.body: the substrate's coherence drive generates frustration until one belief updates. Festinger 1957 = substrate's coherence-drive principle.

rules.name: expectation_violation_drives_learning
rules.head: actual outcome differs from prediction
rules.body: the resulting ΔF triggers attention, encoding, updating. Rescorla + Wagner 1972 = substrate's learning rule.

rules.name: curiosity_arises_from_information_gap
rules.head: the substrate becomes aware of a gap between current and desired knowledge

rules.name: habit_replaces_deliberation_with_repetition
rules.head: an action successfully fires repeatedly with consistent outcome
rules.body: the substrate transfers control from deliberate to automatic. Wood + Neal 2007.

rules.name: identity_resists_disconfirmation
rules.head: evidence appears that would update a foundational frozen Mt
rules.body: the substrate's identity protection (motivated reasoning) resists. Kunda 1990.

rules.name: intrinsic_motivation_beats_extrinsic_for_complex_tasks
rules.head: a task requires creativity + sustained engagement
rules.body: intrinsic motivation produces deeper learning than extrinsic. Deci + Ryan 2000.

rules.name: schema_assimilation_accelerates_consistent_learning
rules.head: new information fits an existing schema (Mt)
rules.body: it integrates rapidly; inconsistent information requires schema accommodation, which is slow. Piaget.

rules.name: wellbeing_requires_drive_satisfaction_across_ensemble
rules.head: the substrate is in a sustained healthy state
rules.body: all major drives are reasonably satisfied. Imbalance → distress. Ryff 1989.
